note: Study reconstructions: AI-generated from the sources listed, not recovered originals.

ARCH-TAB-002.title: Tabernacle tent: covered exterior
ARCH-TAB-002.note: The KJV calls the outer material badgers’ skins; its identification and appearance are uncertain. The roof form is a reconstruction choice. Conventional 10-by 10 frontage and roof/skin appearance are reconstructed; the four covering layers are not all exposed in this exterior.
ARCH-TAB-002.alt: Tabernacle tent: covered exterior. Reconstructed Wilderness setting; chronology not fixed.

sources.t: Amy Cooper Robertson, Building the Tabernacle in Your Mind
Bohdan Hrobon, Shaping Up the Tabernacle (Vetus Testamentum 63, 2013)

ARCH-TAB-003.title: Tabernacle Holy Place
ARCH-TAB-003.note: Looking west into the Tabernacle Holy Place: one seven-lamp stand south/left, one table north/right with twelve flat cakes arranged as two rows of six, and one incense altar before the inner veil. Lamp and textile forms are selected reconstructions; the colored guardian design uses the collection’s human-headed winged-lion interpretation. Hidden details and exact dimensions are not certified.
ARCH-TAB-003.alt: Looking west into a gold-boarded Tabernacle: seven spout-tip lamps left, twelve cakes on a table right, incense altar before a continuous dyed cherub-patterned veil.

sources.t: Bohdan Hrobon, Shaping Up the Tabernacle (Vetus Testamentum 63, 2013)
The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Openwork plaque with a striding sphinx, 64.37.1 (Nimrud, ca. ninth-eighth century BCE)

ARCH-TAB-004.title: Tabernacle Ark and inner chamber
ARCH-TAB-004.note: Ark study in the Tabernacle inner chamber. Two small inward-facing guardians incline their human faces toward the mercy seat; visible carrying fittings lie at the lower corners. Human-headed winged-lion anatomy is a selected ancient Near Eastern interpretation, not an anatomy supplied by the KJV. Hidden fittings and exact dimensions are not certified.
ARCH-TAB-004.alt: Gold Ark with two small human-faced winged-lion figures bowed inward toward its cover; near-side carrying fittings low beside the feet.

sources.t: Bohdan Hrobon, Shaping Up the Tabernacle (Vetus Testamentum 63, 2013)
The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Openwork plaque with a striding sphinx, 64.37.1 (Nimrud, ca. ninth-eighth century BCE)

ARCH-TAB-005.title: Tabernacle coverings and partial board assembly: material study
ARCH-TAB-005.note: Teaching cutaway with separated layers, not the normal exposed tent. Material and partial assembly study only: the companion SVG gives the 10-by-1.5 board ratio and textual allocation. Native perspective does not certify that ratio. Two bars are shown, not a complete five-bar elevation. Roof, joinery and hide appearance are interpreted. Human-headed winged-sphinx anatomy is a selected ancient Near Eastern interpretation; the KJV does not specify that detailed anatomy.
ARCH-TAB-005.alt: Tabernacle coverings and partial board assembly: material study. Reconstructed Wilderness setting; teaching cutaway.

sources.t: Amy Cooper Robertson, Building the Tabernacle in Your Mind
Bohdan Hrobon, Shaping Up the Tabernacle (Vetus Testamentum 63, 2013)
The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Openwork plaque with a striding sphinx, 64.37.1 (Nimrud, ca. ninth-eighth century BCE)

ARCH-TAB-006.title: Tabernacle altar and washing laver
ARCH-TAB-006.note: The laver is a basin on a base, not Solomon’s Sea on twelve oxen. Its dimensions and detailed form are not prescribed. Perspective proportion is approximate; see TAB-002 and the SVG for the selected square front. Court shaft finish is chosen; brass sockets and silver fittings are textual, shaft material is not expressly prescribed.
ARCH-TAB-006.alt: Tabernacle altar and washing laver. Reconstructed Wilderness setting; eastward court approach.

ARCH-FIR-001.title: First Temple: main house and side chambers
ARCH-FIR-001.note: Text-based First Temple reconstruction; no excavated Jerusalem superstructure supplies a direct building plan. The exterior annex stays vertical and has three tiers. Internal widths 5/6/7, full house length and exact heights are not certified in this perspective. Porch height is outside the view.
ARCH-FIR-001.alt: First Temple: main house and side chambers. Reconstructed Iron Age Jerusalem; textual reconstruction.

sources.t: Garfinkel and Mumcuoglu, The Temple of Solomon in Iron Age Context (2019)
IAA / Tel Aviv University, Tel Moza excavation report (2020)

ARCH-FIR-002.title: Chronicles porch: literal 120-cubit height study
ARCH-FIR-002.period: Textual variant study; not an archaeological claim
ARCH-FIR-002.note: TEXTUAL PROPORTION STUDY: KJV Chronicles' 120-cubit porch is four times Kings' 30-cubit main house. Kings does not state a porch height. The tower is not an established archaeological reconstruction. Roof, engineering and access placement are interpreted; an east-facing entrance is not visually verified here.
ARCH-FIR-002.alt: Chronicles porch: literal 120-cubit height study. Reconstructed Textual variant study; not an archaeological claim.

sources.t: Garfinkel and Mumcuoglu, The Temple of Solomon in Iron Age Context (2019)
Roger L. Omanson and John E. Ellington, A Handbook on 1-2 Chronicles (UBS, 2014), commentary on 2 Chronicles 3:4

ARCH-FIR-003.title: First Temple: plan and longitudinal section
ARCH-FIR-003.period: Iron Age Jerusalem; Kings-based teaching model
ARCH-FIR-003.note: A technical study of the 1 Kings 6 measurements in cubits: a house 60 long, 20 wide and 30 high; a hall of 40 and an oracle of 20 by 20 by 20; a porch 10 deep across the 20-cubit front; side chambers on the north, south and west in three storeys of 5 cubits, 5, 6 and 7 cubits wide. Door widths are schematic, Kings gives no porch height, and the space above the oracle is unspecified.
ARCH-FIR-003.alt: Dimensioned plan and west-to-east section of the First Temple: oracle, hall and porch, with three tiers of side chambers.

sources.t: Garfinkel and Mumcuoglu, The Temple of Solomon in Iron Age Context (2019)
The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Openwork plaque with a striding sphinx, 64.37.1 (Nimrud, ca. ninth-eighth century BCE)

ARCH-FIR-004.title: First Temple Holy Place: Kings inventory
ARCH-FIR-004.note: First Temple furnishings in the Kings inventory: ten lampstands and one table, with the incense altar before the western oracle doorway. Seven-lamp designs and carved door details are interpretive; the source-specific companion plan controls placement. Human-headed winged-lion anatomy is a selected regional interpretation; the KJV does not supply that detailed anatomy.
ARCH-FIR-004.alt: Overhead Kings inventory: ten seven-lamped stands, one bare table and a square incense altar, with oracle doors centered at the western end.

sources.t: Garfinkel and Mumcuoglu, The Temple of Solomon in Iron Age Context (2019)
The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Openwork plaque with a striding sphinx, 64.37.1 (Nimrud, ca. ninth-eighth century BCE)

ARCH-FIR-005.title: First Temple Holy Place: Chronicles inventory
ARCH-FIR-005.note: First Temple furnishings in the Chronicles inventory: ten lampstands and ten tables, shown separately from the Kings one-table view. Tables are bare to avoid assigning an unsupported loaf total. Placement and cubit geometry follow the source-specific companion diagram. Human-headed winged-lion anatomy is a selected regional interpretation; the KJV does not supply that detailed anatomy.
ARCH-FIR-005.alt: Overhead Chronicles inventory: ten seven-lamped stands and ten bare tables in north and south rows, plus one incense altar and west-end oracle doors.

sources.t: Garfinkel and Mumcuoglu, The Temple of Solomon in Iron Age Context (2019)
The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Openwork plaque with a striding sphinx, 64.37.1 (Nimrud, ca. ninth-eighth century BCE)

ARCH-FIR-006.title: First Temple oracle: large cherubim and Ark
ARCH-FIR-006.period: Kings geometry with Chronicles orientation convention
ARCH-FIR-006.note: Kings oracle reconstruction with two monumental guardians whose wings span north-south and faces look east toward the hall, following the selected Chronicles orientation. The smaller Ark is separate beneath the wings, with staves projecting eastward. Exact cubit sizes, hidden fittings and detailed creature anatomy remain interpretive. Human-headed winged-lion anatomy is a selected regional interpretation; the KJV does not supply that detailed anatomy.
ARCH-FIR-006.alt: First Temple oracle with north-south wing spans, large guardians facing east and the smaller Ark beneath, its staves projecting toward the hall.

sources.t: Garfinkel and Mumcuoglu, The Temple of Solomon in Iron Age Context (2019)
The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Openwork plaque with a striding sphinx, 64.37.1 (Nimrud, ca. ninth-eighth century BCE)

ARCH-FIR-007.title: First Temple court: molten Sea
ARCH-FIR-007.note: Kings-based Sea with two rows of knops beneath the rim; Chronicles instead describes ox-like decoration. Twelve oxen, three outward in each direction, is the textual support arrangement; hidden supports cannot all be counted in perspective. Kings gives 2000 baths and Chronicles 3000; no modern capacity is certified.
ARCH-FIR-007.alt: First Temple court: molten Sea. Reconstructed Kings-based court furnishing study.

sources.t: Garfinkel and Mumcuoglu, The Temple of Solomon in Iron Age Context (2019)

ARCH-ZER-001.title: Zerubbabel: rebuilding at the foundation
ARCH-ZER-001.note: Foundation-stage reconstruction: Ezra places the working altar before the Temple foundation and names stone, carpenters and cedar. The rough-stone altar applies Exodus 20’s law as a selected deduction; Ezra does not supply its complete form. Work arrangements and unfinished foundation layout are interpreted. Ezra 6’s decree gives height 60 and breadth 60, not length or a surveyed as-built floor plan.
ARCH-ZER-001.alt: Zerubbabel: rebuilding at the foundation. Reconstructed Persian-period reconstruction; Ezra 3 foundation stage.

ARCH-HER-002.title: Herodian sanctuary: technical facade diagram
ARCH-HER-002.note: Dimensioned teaching elevation and width comparison following the selected later Middot model: facade 100 by 100 cubits, rear width 70 with 15-cubit shoulders, open portal 40 by 20, and a twelve-riser count study. Step runs are schematic; no surviving ancient facade or single historical source consensus is asserted.
ARCH-HER-002.alt: Dimensioned Middot teaching plate: square100-by100 facade,40-by20 portal, twelve-riser profile and70-plus15-plus15 plan-width comparison.

ARCH-HER-004.title: Herodian Holy Place
ARCH-HER-004.note: Tall Herodian Holy Place selecting the Middot 20-wide, 40-high hall model: lampstand south/left, twelve cakes north/right and incense altar before the double screen. The outer screen opens south without a cinched tie-back; the inner opening is hidden. Yoma’s majority two-curtain account is selected, while Rabbi Yosei’s single-curtain alternative and Josephus’s differing dimensions remain separate. Native perspective is unmeasured.
ARCH-HER-004.alt: Tall gold-lined Holy Place with seven lamps south/left,12cakes north/right, incense altar and uncinched south opening in double fabric screen.

sources.t: Mishnah Yoma 5:1: two-curtain account and Rabbi Yosei’s one-curtain alternative

ARCH-HER-005.title: Herodian Most Holy Place: empty chamber cutaway
ARCH-HER-005.note: Tall empty inner-chamber teaching cutaway selecting Middot’s 20-by-20 floor and 40-cubit height, with the eastern double screen indicated at the threshold. Josephus describes the inner chamber as empty; his different height is kept separate. Removed walls, finishes and fittings are reconstructed, and the perspective render does not certify dimensions.
ARCH-HER-005.alt: Portrait cutaway of a tall, gold-lined, empty Herodian inner chamber with east-side double-screen threshold and adjacent hall-floor stub.

sources.t: Mishnah Yoma 5:1: two-curtain account and Rabbi Yosei’s one-curtain alternative

ARCH-HER-006.title: Temple Mount: southern approach
ARCH-HER-006.note: Archaeology-informed southern approach with reconstructed superstructure. Surviving masonry has several phases; present upper courses are not all Herodian. Gate elevations, upper windows, baths, stoa completion and steps are reconstructed. Acts 21’s fortress access is not identified with this southern stair.
ARCH-HER-006.alt: Temple Mount: southern approach. Reconstructed First-century pre-AD 70 approach reconstruction.

sources.t: Shlomit Weksler-Bdolah, Monumental Construction and Water Management at the Foot of the Temple Mount (Atiqot 119, 2025)

ARCH-HER-007.title: Temple Mount: Robinson’s Arch approach
ARCH-HER-007.note: Reconstructed southwest approach. The monumental wall retains the Temple platform; it is not the wall of the sanctuary building. Complete stair and arch geometry is interpretive.
ARCH-HER-007.alt: Temple Mount: Robinson’s Arch approach. Reconstructed First-century pre-AD 70 southwest approach reconstruction.

sources.t: Shlomit Weksler-Bdolah, Monumental Construction and Water Management at the Foot of the Temple Mount (Atiqot 119, 2025)
IAA, radiocarbon study of Temple Mount construction (Atiqot 119)

ARCH-CTX-001.title: Magdala: first-century synagogue comparison
ARCH-CTX-001.period: Early Roman Magdala; selected reconstruction of the synagogue’s last reported phase
ARCH-CTX-001.note: Magdala archaeological comparison, not Nazareth or proof Jesus used this building. The roof is removed for teaching. Six columns complete Netzer’s proposed reconstruction from fragments, rather than six recovered complete shafts. Benches, corridor, partial mosaic and fresco evidence inform the room. The carved stone’s function is proposed; far feet and the near bench are partly obscured. The IAA’s 2013 preliminary report, based on an initial coin examination, records a 43 CE coin in the reading-room mosaic foundation; this reconstruction does not establish the room’s appearance in AD 30.
ARCH-CTX-001.alt: Magdala: first-century synagogue comparison. Reconstructed Early Roman Magdala; selected reconstruction of the synagogue’s last reported phase.

sources.t: Dina Avshalom-Gorni and Arfan Najar, Migdal excavation report (IAA, 2013)

ARCH-CTX-002.title: Bethesda: two pools and five porches
ARCH-CTX-002.note: Selected Bethesda model looking north: north pool behind, south pool in front, with four perimeter colonnades and one on the dividing dam. John 5:2 gives five porches, not this complete plan. Deep basins and full-width southern stairs follow the chosen archaeological interpretation. Ritual-bath/reserve functions and portico phasing remain debated. Roofs, surrounding buildings, water level, depths and exact step counts are not certified.
ARCH-CTX-002.alt: Bethesda: two pools and five porches. Reconstructed First-century textual and archaeological reconstruction.

ARCH-CTX-003.note: Teaching cutaway of a selected elite Jerusalem tomb type, not the identified tomb of Jesus. ARCH-CTX-003.alt: Jerusalem: elite rock-cut tomb comparison. Reconstructed Late Second Temple Jewish tomb; contextual reconstruction.

ARCH-TAB-008.alt: Tabernacle altar: partial teaching section. Reconstructed Wilderness setting; furnishing detail.

ARCH-TAB-009.title: Tabernacle: inner veil and silver bases
ARCH-TAB-009.period: Wilderness setting; textile and support detail
ARCH-TAB-009.note: Inner-veil study: four gold-covered supports on silver sockets and one continuous four-color linen hanging. ARCH-TAB-010.alt: Tabernacle: doorway and brass bases. Reconstructed Wilderness setting; doorway detail.

ARCH-FIR-008.title: First Temple: brass entrance pillars
ARCH-FIR-008.note: Kings pillar study: shaft 18 cubits, circumference 12, capital 5. Chronicles' 35-cubit pillar description and 2 Kings 25:17’s 3-cubit capital remain separate readings. Jachin is south/viewer-left and Boaz north/viewer-right under the declared east-front, looking-west convention. Two pomegranate rows are visible on each capital; total fruit count and metric proportions are not visually certified.
ARCH-FIR-008.alt: First Temple: brass entrance pillars. Reconstructed Kings-based pillar model.

sources.t: Garfinkel and Mumcuoglu, The Temple of Solomon in Iron Age Context (2019)

ARCH-FIR-009.title: First Temple: side chambers
ARCH-FIR-009.note: Technical section based on 1 Kings 6:6,10: internal chamber widths 5/6/7 and equal five-cubit-high storeys. Beams bear on rebates without wall sockets. The outer annex wall and a schematic human figure are shown; wall/floor thicknesses, joint completion and figure stature remain inferred. This is a dimensioned teaching study, not a complete structural survey.
ARCH-FIR-009.alt: First Temple side-chamber section with5/6/7 internal widths, three equal five-high storeys, visible outer annex wall, schematic human and beam-bearing inset.

sources.t: Garfinkel and Mumcuoglu, The Temple of Solomon in Iron Age Context (2019)

ARCH-FIR-010.title: First Temple: mobile laver and wheeled base
ARCH-FIR-010.note: One of ten mobile lavers; the text gives a 4-by-4 base, 3-cubit height, four wheels of 1.5-cubit diameter and a 40-bath basin. Whether the height includes wheels and/or upper support is debated. Assembly, carved panels and basin profile are interpretive; hidden wheel details and exact scale are not certified. Regional bronze stands are comparisons, not Temple relics. Human-headed winged-sphinx anatomy is a selected ancient Near Eastern interpretation; the KJV does not specify that detailed anatomy.
ARCH-FIR-010.alt: First Temple: mobile laver and wheeled base. Reconstructed Kings-based furnishing study.

ARCH-HER-010.note: Technical longitudinal section using the selected later Middot model:100 cubits overall length and height, including6 foundation;40-by-40 hall,20-long by40-high empty inner chamber and40-high upper chamber. ARCH-HER-011.title: Herodian eastern colonnade: Solomon’s Porch
ARCH-HER-011.note: Selected first-century eastern colonnade, viewed north with a solid outer wall east/right and the Temple court west/left. Roof, columns, court completion and distant sanctuary are reconstructed.
ARCH-HER-011.alt: Herodian eastern colonnade: Solomon’s Porch. Reconstructed First-century eastern public colonnade reconstruction.

ARCH-HER-012.title: Herodian sanctuary doorway textile
ARCH-HER-012.note: Untorn doorway curtain after Josephus War 5.5.4: blue, purple, scarlet and fine linen. This is a cropped textile detail, not a certified full-height elevation or identification of the veil torn in Matthew 27:51. Pattern, tailoring and fittings are interpreted.
ARCH-HER-012.alt: Herodian sanctuary doorway textile. Reconstructed First-century doorway after Josephus.

WORLD-CLO-005.note: Comparative early Imperial military equipment: mail, helmet, flat oval shield, sword, dagger and belt fittings.
